message.content:
I don’t have real‑time data, but you can quickly check the current air quality in Los Angeles using a few reliable sources:

| Source | How to use it | What you’ll see |
|--------|---------------|-----------------|
| **AirNow** (EPA) | Go to [airnow.gov](https://www.airnow.gov/), enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code. | Current AQI value, pollutant breakdown (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, O₃, NO₂, CO), and health advisories. |
| **AQICN** (World Air Quality Index) | Visit [aqicn.org](https://aqicn.org/city/los-angeles/). | Live AQI, trend graph, and forecast for the next 24 h. |
| **Local news apps** (e.g., LA Times, KABC) | Search “LA air quality” in the app’s news feed. | Often include a quick snapshot and any alerts. |
| **Weather apps** (e.g., Weather.com, AccuWeather) | Look for the “Air Quality” section. | AQI and pollutant levels, plus health recommendations. |

**Quick tip:** If the AQI is 100–150, it’s “Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups.” Above 150 is “Unhealthy,” and above 200 is “Very Unhealthy.” If you’re planning outdoor activities, it’s wise to check the forecast for the next few hours.

If you’d like a quick snapshot right now, let me know and I can guide you through the steps on a specific platform!
